source_refs.claim_scope: Sceye ST1 mission dates, approximately 30-day trans-Pacific return journey, nearly 30,000 km, more than seven days of Japanese operation; Sceye's release describes the vehicle as an unmanned free balloon.
SoftBank's report of the LTA-type Sceye HAPS Japan trial, communications tests, HAPS-to-drone communications and approximately 5 km station-keeping radius.
Independent reporting on the 30-day Japan round trip and the trade between buoyant LTA payload/solar-area potential and fixed-wing endurance/steering capability.
Sceye's platform-level design propositions and manufacturer-stated 425 Wh/kg lithium-sulphur battery energy density; not an independently verified installed-pack specification.

owner_work_refs.responsibility: HAPS-specific service boundary, buoyant-versus-fixed-wing comparison and energy-service benchmark.
Whole-aircraft architecture portfolio and matched mission MDO.
Aircraft/energy co-design and mission-matched energy architecture comparison.
Coverage/network scheduling and cross-layer service evidence.
Solar generation, storage and persistent-platform energy accounting where the buoyant platform energy boundary applies.
Envelope, solar array, battery, payload, inspection and maintenance configuration provenance.

unknowns.reason: No as-built envelope geometry, volume, pressure regulation, ballonets, hull mass or material allowables are supplied.
No buoyancy margin, gas management, thermal expansion or altitude-control model is bound.
No propulsion or wind-relative trajectory model, station-keeping energy trace, control authority or wind-regime applicability receipt is supplied.
No as-built array area, flexible-lamination mass, attitude/incidence, shading or temperature map is bound.
Manufacturer-level energy-density statements are not an installed pack specification; no pack mass, usable energy, pressure/temperature behavior, ageing or thermal model is supplied.
No verified payload mass, continuous/peak power, RF or optical payload duty cycle, cooling or service-quality budget is supplied.
Public mission durations and area-stationing intervals do not define the complete wind, geography, seasonal or service availability envelope.
No handling infrastructure, recovery method, pressure-hull inspection, gas replenishment, repair turnaround or fleet spares plan is bound.
No HAPS-to-aircraft power-transfer source/receiver, net surplus, end-to-end efficiency or in-flight energy service has been demonstrated by these references.
No jurisdiction-specific airspace, spectrum, safety, site or operating authority is implied by public demonstration reports.

assumptions: This is a reference architecture record for the buoyant lighter-than-air HAPS class, not a Sceye aircraft digital twin or a Luminous Dynamics design.

The ST1 record is classified as a buoyant HAPS with free-balloon subtype because Sceye's mission release describes it as an unmanned free balloon; the record does not assume an airship propulsion system.

Sceye ST1's approximately 30-day trans-Pacific round trip and more than seven days over Japan are distinct from Sceye's earlier SE2 12-day endurance programme and its reported 88+ hours at selected areas. These results are not merged into one platform configuration or station-keeping duration.
SoftBank's reported HAPS-to-drone result concerns communications and data links, not wireless energy transfer.

Sceye's platform website states a 425 Wh/kg lithium-sulphur battery energy density and months-to-a-year design ambition. Those remain manufacturer claims and are not independently verified installed-pack data or a demonstrated year-long flight.

The 2026 Sceye mission reports are source-attributed operational evidence; exact mass, payload, solar area, power, wind/positioning trace, thermal profile, fuel/gas usage, duty cycle and life-cycle data remain unknown.
No fixed-wing-versus-buoyant performance winner is asserted. Architecture selection must use the same service, weather, coverage, payload, reserve, reliability and cost boundaries.
All unreported physical properties, model outputs and operational permissions remain unknown.
